Now a force F directed downward along the inclined plane is used to push the object, making it move downward along the inclined plane with uniform acceleration. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an inclined plane body placed on horizontal ground; the ground is drawn with horizontal lines and oblique-line shading; the inclined plane slopes upward to the right, and the object m is placed on the inclined plane; the figure also marks a force F acting on the object along the direction of the inclined plane. Let the inclination angle of the inclined plane be θ. Reasoning: Originally the object m can slide down along the inclined plane body at uniform speed, indicating that the resultant force along the direction of the inclined plane is zero. The component of the object's gravity downward along the inclined plane is mg sinθ, and the sliding friction force is upward along the inclined plane, with magnitude f, so there is f = mg sinθ. In the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane there is no acceleration, and the support force N = mg cosθ, so f/N = tanθ. Now apply another force F downward along the inclined plane. Because F is along the direction of the inclined plane and has no component perpendicular to the inclined plane, the pressure of the object on the inclined plane still satisfies N = mg cosθ, and the magnitude of the sliding friction force is also still f = μN, remaining the same as before. Analyze the forces exerted by the object on the inclined plane body in the horizontal direction: the pressure of the object on the inclined plane body has a horizontal component of magnitude N sinθ; the direction of the friction force of the object on the inclined plane body is opposite to the friction force of the inclined plane on the object, and its horizontal component has magnitude f cosθ, in a direction opposite to the horizontal component of the pressure. From the original uniform-speed condition f/N = tanθ, it can be obtained that f cosθ = N sinθ, so these two horizontal components exactly cancel. Therefore, the inclined plane body has no tendency to move horizontally relative to the ground, and the horizontal ground does not need to provide a friction force on the inclined plane body.
